title: The five-rung Science guide is a set of paragraphs, not a ladder you can climb -- every rung opens an explanation and a 'Got it' button with no action
repairSummary: Rung 2 ('Pick a target') was still routed through onJumpToPhotometry, which the populated tab answered with a scroll to the PHOTOMETRY charts (plots + AAVSO export + period panel, no target control) and the all-empty tab answered by opening the photometric calibration wizard. Added ScienceLadderCard.onPickTarget, routed ScienceRung.track to it, and wired both branches of science_analytics_tab.dart to a new _goPickPhotometryTarget() that turns on scienceModeStateProvider.scienceHudVisible and GoRouter.maybeOf(context)?.go('/imaging') -- the science HUD is the only control in the app that calls SciencePhotometrySelectionNotifier.setTarget. The empty branch's onJumpToPhotometry (the locked-rung 'Go to photometry' unlock and rungs 3/4 CTAs) now goes there too instead of opening the calibration wizard. New test packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_ladder_pick_target_test.dart drives the real ScienceAnalyticsTab under a GoRouter on both branches.
reasoning: The fixer's narrow claim is fully present and correct: science_ladder_card.dart:23 declares onRunCalibration, :176 routes ScienceRung.measure to it, and BOTH ScienceLadderCard call sites (science_analytics_tab.dart:583 empty branch, :636 populated branch -- the only two in the repo) pass () => _openCalibrationWizard(context), which showDialogs PhotometricCalibrationWizard at :145. The headline finding is indeed stale: _actions in science_rung_sheet.dart:112-150 returns spec.ctaLabel for ready and 'Jump to it' for done, and the two gate strings it quotes are gone from _prerequisiteFor. But the fix is INCOMPLETE against the finding it answers, by the fixer's own stated rule ('named for the action, so a host cannot quietly answer it with a scroll'): rung 2's button says 'Pick a target' and _runCta sent it to onJumpToPhotometry, which is a scroll to a chart section on the populated branch and the photometric CALIBRATION wizard on the empty branch -- the same defect shape, in the same widget, on the first-run surface the on-ramp exists for. Two further corrections to the summary: (a) 'the calibration wizard became unreachable from anywhere in the app' is false -- _PhotometricTransformsCard renders in the same populated branch at science_analytics_tab.dart:909 with a 'Calibrate' button that opens the identical dialog; the defect was a lying button, not an unreachable feature. (b) The unlockLabel/onUnlock additions in science_rung_sheet.dart belong to a different fix, not this one.
evidence: Severed the wiring, not the logic (fixer's fix): replaced science_analytics_tab.dart:636 onRunCalibration with the old () => _jumpTo(_sectionKeys.fieldQuality). science_ladder_run_calibration_test.dart went red ('Found 0 widgets with type PhotometricCalibrationWizard'); restored, green. Severed my repair the same way: reverted onPickTarget to _openCalibrationWizard (empty) / _jumpTo(_sectionKeys.photometry) (populated) -- all 3 new tests went red ('Found 1 widget with type PhotometricCalibrationWizard' and 'Found 0 widgets with text IMAGING SCREEN'); restored, 10/10 green across the four ladder suites. The rename alone gives no compile-time protection (onRunCalibration: () => _jumpTo(...) still compiles), so the test is what holds the wiring.

title: The Submit-discovery dialog opens on TNS even when TNS is unusable and another network is ready
reasoning: The claim is present and is the real mechanism. git diff vs HEAD shows the shipped code was `TransientReportFormat _format = TransientReportFormat.tns;` with no re-evaluation anywhere; the working tree adds `_format = _resolveFormat(selected, scienceSettings);` at transient_report_panel.dart:79 and `_resolveFormat` at :240-254 with exactly the described semantics (keep the current selection while _formatEnabled, else first enabled in the shipped tns/aavso/mpc order, else leave alone). Not disclosure-only: the primary button itself flips from a dead 'Submit to TNS' to a live 'Export report' (:325-339) and the chip selection moves, so behaviour changed, not wording. Not incomplete across surfaces: TransientReportPanel is the ONLY format-owning widget -- the two callers, science_export_hub.dart:802 and first_light/widgets/transient_submit_dialog.dart:45 (the 'Submit discovery' dialog the finding names), both embed it and hold no format state of their own, so one fix covers both. Not inverted: when nothing is usable the selection stays on TNS and the TNS blocker is the one named (second test). One residual I checked and judged harmless: _resolveFormat runs on the first frame, when sessionFrameCalibrationsProvider is still loading, so the AAVSO zeropoint is null and a late-arriving calibration cannot pull the selection back off a lower-preference network it already latched onto. That can only bite when TNS is unconfigured (TNS gates on credentials alone, so it never loses a race), which reduces the case to aavso-vs-mpc -- and MPC only enables for TransientKind.movingStreak (transient_candidate.dart:50), i.e. exactly the detection for which MPC is the right network. No user-visible wrong outcome, so not a defect.
evidence: Severed the wiring, not the logic: commented out transient_report_panel.dart:79 (`_format = _resolveFormat(...)`) leaving _resolveFormat itself intact. transient_report_default_network_test.dart went red at line 81 -- 'opens on the network that works, not on a blocked TNS' failed on `expect(find.text('Submit to TNS'), findsNothing)`, i.e. the panel fell back to the dead TNS button. Restored; 7/7 green across transient_report_default_network_test.dart, transient_report_reasons_test.dart and transient_report_panel_calibration_test.dart.

title: The 'AstroBin' export produces JSON + Markdown, not the acquisition CSV AstroBin imports, and omits the observation date entirely
repairSummary: stack_result_screen.dart:914 passed the un-awaited Future to a DateTime? parameter. Replaced with `final acquisitionDate = await _acquisitionDate(result); if (!mounted) return;` and passed the resolved value. Also fixed the fix's own test, stack_result_astrobin_date_test.dart, which gave its scope inMemoryDatabaseOverride() and then hit the drift `!timersPending` teardown assertion: added the `settleProviderTeardown(tester)` call from test/harness/provider_teardown.dart plus an exact-row assertion (`'2026-05-28,18,300'`). Both files dart-formatted.
reasoning: All three sub-claims are literally present and correct at the service layer: exportAstroBinAcquisition (stack_share_export_service.dart:425-461) branches on p.extension -- .csv writes toAstroBinCsv(), .json the indented payload, anything else the <base>.md block, with the Markdown always written alongside; AstroBinExportMetadata gained date + dateIso (stack_and_share_models.dart:790, :806-812) rendered into toMarkdown/toJson/toAstroBinCsv; the picker asks for csv first (stack_result_screen.dart:902-906). BUT the production call site did not compile. `_acquisitionDate` returns Future<DateTime?> and buildAstroBinMetadata takes DateTime?, and the fixer wrote `acquisitionDate: _acquisitionDate(result)` with no await. `flutter analyze lib/screens/stack_result/stack_result_screen.dart` reported exactly one error: "The argument type 'Future<DateTime?>' can't be assigned to the parameter type 'DateTime?' ... :914:26 argument_type_not_assignable". That is a hard compile failure in skotiq_app's lib, so the desktop/mobile app could not be built at all and every test importing StackResultScreen (including stack_result_screen_test.dart and the fix's own stack_result_astrobin_date_test.dart) failed to load. The fix's own test therefore cannot have been run green by its author -- and once it compiled it still failed, on the known drift zero-duration-timer teardown assertion. Sub-claim (2), the date, was thus shipped entirely non-functional; sub-claims (1) and (3) held only in the service, which nothing reachable could call. Two smaller residuals I checked and did NOT count against it: exportAstroBinAcquisition falls back to Markdown when toAstroBinCsv() returns null, but StackAndShareResult.createdAt is non-nullable and buildAstroBinMetadata always sets `date: acquisitionDate ?? result.createdAt`, so the UI path can never hit it; and `ref.read(allSessionsProvider.future)` is safe because allSessionsProvider (database_provider.dart:139) is a plain StreamProvider, not autoDispose, so the element is not vacuumed before the stream emits. Whether AstroBin's importer accepts a bare date,number,duration header is not verifiable from here -- no network -- so that specific claim is taken on the fixer's word.
evidence: Compile error reproduced and then cleared: `flutter analyze lib/screens/stack_result/stack_result_screen.dart` -> 1 error at :914:26 before the repair, 'No issues found!' after. Severed the wiring, not the logic: replaced the repaired call with `service.buildAstroBinMetadata(result: result)` (dropping the acquisitionDate argument, leaving _acquisitionDate and the whole CSV/date pipeline intact). stack_result_astrobin_date_test.dart went red with "Expected: a string starting with '2026-05-28' / Actual: '2026-08-09,18,300'" -- i.e. the restack day, the exact defect. Restored; green. skotiq_core test/services/stack_share_export_service_test.dart + test/models/imaging/stack_and_share_models_test.dart + test/services/stack_and_share_service_test.dart: 80/80 passed. Final confirmation run: stack_result_astrobin_date_test.dart + stack_result_screen_test.dart + transient_report_default_network_test.dart + the two science-ladder suites -> 17/17 green.
